<Rep. Jamie Raskin>: I oppose H.R. 1468, which would reestablish the discredited and discriminatory ``China Initiative'' at the Department of Justice (DOJ). The sponsors of this bill invite us all to participate in some magical thinking. They want us to pretend the China Initiative didn't happen during the last Trump Administration. They want us to pretend the China Initiative wasn't a total failure.
They want us to pretend the first China Initiative didn't result in Chinese researchers at American universities being targeted for simple paperwork errors just so the DOJ could finally prosecute someone and claim a victory, even though many of the cases were dismissed or overturned on appeal.\1\ And my Republican colleagues want us to pretend that if we change the name just a little bit--from ``the China Initiative'' to ``the CCP Initiative''--no one will notice that this bill is the same failed enterprise all over again. No matter how hard they pretend, they can't change the past: The anti-Asian hate that proliferated around this country led to nearly 13,000 race-driven acts of hate and crimes against Asian Americans.\2\
\1\Blog Post, Engineering Professor Acquitted in Latest Setback to DOJ's ``China Initiative,'' Arnold & Porter (Sept. 20, 2021), https:// www.arnoldporter.com/en/perspectives/blogs/enforcement-edge/2021/09/ engineering-professor-acquitted.
\2\Report, The State of AA/PI Hate in 2024, STOP AAPI HATE (June 2025), https://stopaapihate.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/25-SAH- StateofHateReport-F-digital.pdf.
This bill is particularly tone deaf because Donald Trump is ceding more global power to China every day. During his first term, Chinese government and state-owned companies spent no less than $5.5 million dollars at Trump properties--to say nothing of the valuable trademarks Chinese authorities rushed to grant him and his family members. In exchange, he opposed sanctions against Chinese telecommunications companies and banks even when they threatened our national security. He even tried to cancel a military exercise with Japan and South Korea because China and Russia complained.
Donald Trump's second term has been more of the same. Over the last 18 months, the Trump Administration has weakened America's soft power abroad by defunding foreign aid programs and closing embassies, hurt America's economy with unlawful and arbitrary tariffs, and hamstrung our ability to respond to threats by firing government workers, including experts on China and national security personnel. He has done all this while using his cryptocurrency ventures to pocket millions of dollars from Chinese billionaires with ties to the Chinese Communist Party (CCP). In May, a tiny Chinese technology company with ties to the Chinese government announced it had bought as much as $300 million of President Trump's memecoin-- despite having no revenue and only eight employees.\3\
\3\Michael Clark, Trump Forfeits U.S. Global Leadership at Americans' Expense and to China's Gain, Ctr. for American Progress (Apr. 17, 2025), https://www.americanprogress.org/article/trump-forfeits-u-s-global-leadership-at-americans-expense-and-to-chinas-gain/.
President Trump's use of his office for personal enrichment is corrupt. But what is possibly even more galling is how President Trump is using Chinese President Xi as a model for leadership. President Trump once referred to President Xi as a ``brilliant guy'' who controls ``1.4 billion people with an iron fist.''\4\ He assured President Xi that sending Uighurs to forced labor camps was ``exactly the right thing to do'' and that violently cracking down on pro-democracy protests in Hong Kong was acting ``very responsibly.''
\4\Blog Post, Representative Quotations from President Trump on President Xi and China, Harvard Univ., https://www.belfercenter.org/ programs/thucydidess-trap/representative-quotations-president-trump-president-xi-and-china.
In his second term in office, President Trump appears to be committed to remaking his Administration in the image of President Xi's regime: cracking down on media outlets he disapproves of, attempting hostile takeovers of the ``ideology'' of colleges and universities, attacking attorneys for representing clients or causes he dislikes, purging libraries, sending masked agents in unmarked vans to arrest foreign students for voicing opinions he disagrees with, shipping people to El Salvador's notorious torture prison, and using artificial intelligence to surveil individuals' social media posts and to create a mega database of Americans' information.
It is no surprise that we are not looking at reasonable, nonpartisan ways to augment national security at the DOJ, because Donald Trump has for over a year now been deconstructing our national security infrastructure, replacing experience with loyalists and common sense with partisan vitriol. Since taking office, Donald Trump has gutted the National Security Division at DOJ and fired thousands of experienced employees at the State Department, draining our agencies of incalculably valuable expertise. He has reassigned a quarter of Federal Bureau of Investigation agents and almost all of the agents at Homeland Security Investigations away from their national security duties and reassigned them to immigration enforcement, including picking up moms and kids with no criminal histories, instead of going after actual terrorists and serious fraudsters.
Donald Trump has left nuclear agreement negotiations to his son-in-law and Steve Witkoff, neither of whom have any experience with nuclear disarmament, and has recalled 30 ambassadors while leaving a whole 80 ambassador positions unfilled--even in key countries in the Middle East. He closed down the Global Engagement Center, the State Department's office tasked with combatting foreign disinformation and influence campaigns. He has jeopardized NATO and weakened strategic partnerships around the world, all while wreaking havoc on our economy with his punitive tariffs, used as a last-ditch effort because he can't actually employ effective international leverage and strategy.
This Administration has no real interest in protecting our national security, from Chinese threats or otherwise. It is up to us, Congress, to take action to protect against strategic threats from China--and this bill does the opposite.
I urge my colleagues to oppose this legislation.
Jamie Raskin,
Ranking Member.
